plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY02 delivering spoken persuasive texts using features of voice; VC2E5LY01 listening for and identifying a speaker's purpose; VC2E5LE02 reflecting on texts
plan.shape: model, deliver, reflect: the teacher delivers the shade-trees speech first, students deliver theirs to a live audience while listeners record each call to action, then everyone reflects
plan.criticalFeature: the audience should know what you want them to do: the call to action lands
decisionPoints: the choice check: which audience knows what to do
the exit board: my call to action and one change
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: say it, for real.
plan.catchUp: Absent or anxious speakers: deliver to a small group or the teacher later in the week.

routineIcons: Point to A, B or C
Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: After each speech: applause, then write their call to action on your board

example.answer: A question that brings back a small story.

items.prompt: Not next year. Not next week. Today.
Last summer, Mia fainted at soccer.
Who here wants a cooler yard?

example.answer: Shade trees; say yes on Tuesday; yes, I knew what to do.

items.prompt: For each speaker, write their position and what they want us to do.

example.answer: Eyes: 2. I looked up for my action but read my story.

items.prompt: Score yourself 1, 2 or 3 and give proof.

example.answer: The ouch hook worked. Next time I'd slow my story down.

items.prompt: What was your best moment today? Why did it work?
items.answer: A specific moment and why it worked.

items.prompt: If you gave your speech again, what would you change?
items.answer: One specific change to writing or delivery.

example.answer: Ouch! That's our slide in summer. Shade cuts UV by 75%. Say yes to trees on Tuesday.

items.prompt: Write a 30-second radio ad version of your speech.
items.answer: A short ad: hook, one strong reason, one action, about 60-75 words.

steps: My action and a polite close
example.answer: Dear Ms Ross, our yard needs shade. It hit 41 degrees. Please plant ten trees. Yours sincerely...

items.prompt: Write a short letter to the real person who can say yes to your speech.
items.answer: A letter with greeting, position, best proof, a clear request and a polite close.

example.answer: My best part was the ouch. Next time I will slow down. I feel proud.

slides.notes: Open Speech Day. One line: today you are the speaker, and the room is your audience.

Print the Speech Day Notes for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported version for those who need it. Speaking order on the board. Large classes: about 2.5 minutes per speaker, so plan a second session.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to deliver a persuasive speech to a live audience.
successCriteria: I can deliver my speech from my cue cards.
I can use eye contact, voice and pauses so my audience knows what to do.
I can reflect on what worked and what I would change.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Four weeks of work. Today, it's yours.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: The audience has a job too
lines: Eyes on the speaker. Still hands. Big applause.
After every speech: write their call to action on your board.

notes.answer: eyes on the speaker, still hands, applause, write the action
beats: SAY: Every speaker deserves the audience you'd want.
ASK: Which audience job is hardest for you? 1 eyes, 2 still hands, 3 applause.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: a mix
ASK: How will you show a nervous speaker you're with them?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: smile; nod; look at them
SAY: Big applause for every speaker, before and after.
trap: listeners rehearsing their own speech instead of listening.
Fix: say cards down while others speak.

slides.meaning: How you say a speech: voice, pace, eyes and body.
slides.example: Great delivery: slow, loud, eyes up.

notes.answer: how you say a speech: voice, pace, eyes and body
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Delivery. Say it with me. Delivery.
SAY: How you say a speech: voice, pace, eyes and body.
SAY: Great delivery: slow, loud, eyes up.
ASK: Name one part of delivery you'll focus on today.
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: eye contact; volume; pauses; slowing down
trap: thinking delivery means saying it fast to get it over with.
Fix: say slow is brave, and slow is clear.

rows: Feet still, card in one hand
In for four, out for four
One friendly face in the middle
My hook, slower than feels normal

notes.answer: plant, breathe, find a face, slow first line
beats: SAY: Watch my ten seconds before I speak.
MODEL each step on the table, then deliver the full shade-trees speech.
POINT to Slow first line.
SAY: Nerves speed you up. So I start slower than feels normal.
SAY: After my speech, write my call to action on your board.
Then we check.
ASK: What did I want you to do?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: say yes to ten trees on Tuesday
trap: starting before the room is quiet.
Fix: say wait for silence; it's yours.
notes.stretch: Use a gesture on your strongest line.
notes.help: Read your first line from the card, then look up.
notes.prep: Teacher delivers first: it lowers the stakes. Critical feature: the call to action lands.

slides.title: Which audience knows what to do?

options.text: A speech that ends: That's all, thanks.
options.misconception: no action; the audience leaves with nothing

options.text: A speech that ends: Switch off one light tonight.
A speech that ends: Polar bears are important.

beats: SAY: Three speeches, three last lines.
ASK: Which audience knows what to do?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: read your own last line.
Less -> ask what would you DO after each? re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Check your own last card now. Is it an action?
trap: pointing to C because it's strong.
Fix: ask what would you do after hearing C?
notes.prep: Decision point before speeches: last check on calls to action. Under 80% means two minutes to fix last cards.

slides.title: Speech Day
lines: Speakers in the order on the board. About 2 minutes each.
After each speech: applause, then boards.
Waiting? Fill in your Speech Day Notes.

notes.answer: open - every speaker delivers; listeners record each call to action
beats: SAY: Speaker one, when you're ready. Take your time.
TIME each speech on the board timer.
RECORD for each speaker: eyes, voice, pace, action landed.
ASK: After each speech, what did they want us to do?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the speaker's call to action
SAY: Name one strength for each speaker, warmly and specifically.
trap: Fix: say breathe, look at your first card. Start again; we're with you.
notes.prep: The main event. Large classes run across two sessions; anxious speakers may present to a small group. SC2.

slides.title: After each speech
slides.pivot: ask the speaker to say their last line again
slides.followUp: cold call one board: how did you know?

items.text: What did the speaker want us to do?
items.expect: the action, in a few words

items.text: What was their position, in five words or fewer?

items.answer: a fact, an expert or a story from the speech

items.expect: the hook in a few words

items.text: Which word did they stress most?
items.answer: a stressed word from the speech
the speaker's small story or image

say: Use one question after each speech. Boards up, then applause again.
trap: boards writing what they liked, not what was said.
Fix: ask what exactly did they say?
notes.stretch: Name the Toolkit move the speaker used.
notes.prep: Rotate these after each speech. Every board shows whether the message landed. SC2.

slides.title: Reflect and record
slides.task: Work through your Speech Day Notes. Finish by reflecting on your own speech.
slides.frame: My best moment was ___. Next time I will ___.

notes.answer: audience notes for each speaker and a specific reflection
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Record each speaker as you go. Reflect when you've spoken.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: what proof do you have for that score?
ASK: Tell your partner your best moment and one change.
30 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: a specific moment and a specific change
trap: a reflection that says it was good.
Fix: student names one exact moment.
notes.stretch: Extension: a radio ad, then a letter to the real decision-maker.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a listening table, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent reflection on their own delivery. SC3.

slides.extendedTask: Speech Day Notes ending in a written reflection on the student's own speech

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Write your own call to action, exactly as you said it.
Then write one change you would make to your delivery.

notes.answer: the student's call to action plus one specific delivery change
beats: SAY: Your own speech. Two lines.
ASK: Write your call to action and one delivery change.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: an action and a specific change
RECORD who has no clear action. Feedback conversation before reports.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 and SC3. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What is one thing you learned about persuading people that you'll keep using?

notes.answer: open - start with a hook; prove it; end with an action
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How proud are you of your speech today?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What is one thing you learned
about persuading people that you'll keep using?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: start with a hook; prove it; end with an action
notes.prep: End of the speech unit. Celebrate every speaker. SC2 and SC3.
